already_hybrid.source: Hasr assumption: hybrid key exchange is already in place, so key exchange needs no migration. Certificates are listed separately; client support is not measured by Hasr and remains for the institution to track.

tls13_classical.source: Hasr assumption: a configuration change or library upgrade within one change cycle.

no_tls13.source: Hasr assumption: a protocol or platform upgrade.

managed_tls_policy.source: Hasr assumption: a policy switch on a managed TLS endpoint, plus client-compatibility testing.

z.source: NIST IR 8547 (final, 27 October 2026): every quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithm (RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, finite-field and elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman) is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035, at every key size. The November 2024 draft deprecated only the 112-bit parameter sets after 2030; the final report removed that distinction. The EU Coordinated Implementation Roadmap (June 2025) sets the end of 2030 for high-risk use cases, including finance. SAMA Circular 482021280 sets no migration date.
